This is written as someone who loves Co-op/PVE multiple thousands of hours in L4D2/PD2 and doesn't normally do anything PVP anymore.  

Having hit max level I feel like it's time to do a review, even though I don't usually like reviewing popular/trending games. I believe this game is finally passed the friendly honey moon peak and will fall off for those who enjoy PVE/cooperative experiences. I feel like the overall vibe of the game has finally shifted to why I have never enjoyed always on PVP games. The Division 1 & 2 are prime examples of this as well where I loved Dark Zone until it just stopped being fun running into people. I ended up playing PVE just so much more in that one. The dynamics are shaping up to be exactly the same in this, but with no coop only experience. The game has serious potential to have a solid PVE mode with how challenging and coordinated the ARC AI is and I'm hoping they put it in at some point. 

Running around and helping people out has stopped being fun as with most of the people it's shoot on sight as opposed to fun personable experiences. I have stopped bringing any equipment except a defib in my safe slot because it's gotten to the point where I just get tired of winning in multiple PVP scenarios only to have a camper on the Raider Hatch or Extraction zone. Then there's the dropping into a match with 17 minutes left, which pretty much solidified me never bringing ANY items in except Defib. Even with no gun and only a Rubber Ducky and saying friendly, people will shoot on site. I've been killed multiple times after rezing people who were asking for help with a matriarch or bastion. Free load out is a great idea but it's been almost every encounter I'm in where that's all people are running. Having played competitive FPS pro back in high school, I've been burnt out on pure PVP shoot on site for a long time and had to say the first few days were very inspiring but it has really been toxic the last few days. Being someone who never shoots first or enjoys PVP that much, it's been really unfortunate. I have already turned off crossplay but even the PC players are mostly shoot on site now. I believe the game has been successful enough that Embark should have enough to develop a different system outside of wipes/different queues for less toxic players or a PVE mode. 

The gameplay is unreal, slightly pun related. Gunplay is great. Climbing & moving translate perfectly to how you want your character to move even in battles. Sound design is just easily best in class (directional audio needs some work on the Z axis) with good headphones where every encounter I had I was never really taken by surprise unless I was really really sloppy. It is nice seeing a UE5 game being so well optimized. I absolutely love the map designs and world design, it is utterly unique and I'm surprised we haven't seen more of the mid 70's - early 80s space futurism aesthetic outside of Deathloop. Embark has something special here and if they play their cards right will have the chance to define the Extraction shooter genre. 

TL:DR An amazing game which is starting to succumb to the toxic shoot on site gameplay of Escape from Tarkov or Hunt Showdown, I have faith in Embark to find a way out but be warned that the game clips you have seen of it being chill in solo's has shifted already. If you enjoy Extraction Shooters, this is a best in class but if you are looking for a more coop chill experience, wait and see what developers do.

Don't get me wrong, I love this game its really fun - when it works. The Dev team only seems to be addressing some issues while sweeping so many crashes and bugs under the rug. I run a 13th Gen Intel i9-13900HX, 2200 Mhz, 24 Cores, 32 Logical Processor, Nvidia Geforce RTX 4090 Laptop GPU, 32GB Ram and 2TB SSD. I am forced to run my game on the LOWEST SETTINGS, Ray Tracing OFF, DLSS OFF. and my computer in a balanced mode just to get this game to run for 15 mins - maximum 1hr before it crashes. The devs have addressed the AMD issue as the AMD community have drawn the shorter straw but Intel are still having issues with nothing resolved. I have been troubleshooting since day 1 and have been active on discord. I have done everything under the sun, run it in DX11, tested my hardware on multiple platforms to find no hardware errors, adjusted my PC, undervolted, overclocked, restored to factory settings, adjusted control panel, adjusted windows security, even going to the lengths of completely wiping my PC, reinstalling windows with no luck, I have even gone and sent crash dumps to professionals AND MORE. 

I know its not just me as I have discussed with many over discord these issues, the game states its reccomended specs so why is it that I am running on LOW and still crashing with much higher specs than the reccomended.
The DEVS give no updates on crashes and issues, just only posting about community events for those who have been lucky enough to not run into any issues. 

This review will turn to a positive one once these issues are addressed because I am loving this game when I can play it but until then I'll just have to wait. (I have even considered buying a completely new PC haha but a game isn't worth a completely new PC nor did I sign up to get my masters in troubleshooting and PC engineering)

I'll be honest: I'm not the biggest fan of extraction shooters. I've had multiple experiences with them, and the only one to this date that kept me hooked for hours on end was the cycle: frontier. But this game? I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love it! The community, though might seem a bit toxic at first, is incredibly friendly. The way how everyone is interracting with each other brings me so much joy, as I haven't had any other game bring such an experience. Where else can you bundle up a 7 man of solos and go killing a jumper for a random's quest, only for them to die from it and miss the quest :'D

Pros of this game:
 * The sound design in this game bring me eargasm
 * Guns, explosives, grenades, etc. feel like they're actually doing something instead of just being props
 * The community has "fractions", if you could call them that, which fit any player's taste! We got pvp one-tricks, we got chill people, we even have anti-camp groups! And the community did it all by themselves!
 * Map design has always been my passion in gaming, and this game absolutely DELIVERED. The maps, feel big, but also not too big so you can still run across the entire map, while having fun blasting ARCs and being mesmerised by the landscapes.

Cons of this game: 
 * Audio feels very weird sometimes? You can clearly hear someone but you can't tell if you're above or below them. - might be resolved later tho!! when it is i'll edit this
 * The weaponry, while powerful, seem a bit too... overpowered. I personally think that there should be a bit more balancing to them. (This didn't impact the amount of fun I had with the game though!)

Overall, I think you should check out this game. If you're not too confident about buying it - I can assure you that you'll definitely know your answer in 1.5-2 hours of playtime steam gives you to refund the game.

[h1]Minor Gripe[/h1]
The skill tree is fun. Unfortunately, there is only one way to reset skills right now. I understand this from a design perspective: It makes player choice important and meaningful. Players need to consider playstyle and focus, rather than hop from meta to meta. The skill point cap is way less than completely filling up the tree, so you can't have it all. Lots of games have skill trees, and it is a great mechanic in most cases.
[h2]Two problems here[/h2]
[h3]Newb Trap[/h3]
Players get skill points immediately. The mobile game style yellow "unread" notifications compels us to use the skill points ASAP. This is truly a "skill issue" and the player is at fault for pressing buttons without knowing what they do. The devs are also at fault for setting up this precarious situation. Devs can't stop players from being stupid, but certain pitfalls can be avoided and mistakes can turn into lessons learned.
[h3]Balance Patches[/h3]
The devs make balance changes for the sake of the game. This is important. The problem: Players aren't able to refund or reallocate skills after these changes. We don't need a complete skill tree wipe every week, because wasp damage was increased 2%, Kettle arc armor penetration was increased etc. The focused nature of this skill tree can make these tiny changes immense in some cases.
[h1]Major Gripe[/h1]
$20 outfits in a $40 game. Over $200 worth of skins in the cash shop on launch. This game is not worth the $250 (and rising) price tag.
[h3]bUt tHeY aRe eArNaBlE fReE tO pLaY[/h3]
If there is an option to swipe, then the devs will make earning the item tedious.
[h3]bUt yOu dOn'T nEeD eVeRy sKiN[/h3]
Why are the devs spending time and resources developing things I will never get to use? It adds more incentive to spend time on cosmetics rather than the game.
[h3]bUt [i]Other Game[/i] dOeS iT[/h3]
Yes, those games are also flawed.
[h1]38 hours later...[/h1]
The voice acting in this game is [b]bad[/b]. Every single line is delivered with the same confident, boring tone. Somber dialog? Naw, just deliver it like all the rest! Most traders hide there expression while they talk (or are an android). Celeste sticks out as being particularly poorly voiced, because the character is staring at the camera. And these traders never stop talking! Staying on the shop window means hearing these lines every 15 seconds. I dread opening the store. The intercom voices are also insufferable. Both the voice acting, AND the writing! It's extremely snarky, compared to the desperate tone of the game world.

Risk vs. Reward balance is just sweet. Absolutely addicting gameplay loop. Matches can be 5 minutes - quick in & out grab some stuff quick and get out, or you can push it and get sweaty trying to live. Always fair, sometimes infuriating, and always a good time. PC players are far more civil than console, I turned crossplay off after 20 hours and am having a much better time.

There is extraction shooters and then there is ARC Raiders.

For whatever reason, maybe it's a mix of the proximity chat, the PvPvE, or just the way the ARC will adapt to the strategies you use to kill them, but this game has literally hooked me back into being a gamer. Finally something that is connecting me to other people.

A lot of players are saying the community is toxic. This is far from the truth. I've ran into few toxic players, at least going Solo. Even in Duos there isn't that much. Some say the console players are the main culprits, but what I love is the choice to do these things.

Do I get pissed when I'm at a EVAC and someone that I've been running there with decides to blast me in the back... absolutely. But that's the part about this game that keeps me on edge, every run, every time. I wouldn't want the devs to change the way the game is at all. Just my opinion.

Walking up to someone and hearing them go "Friendly, Friendly, you cool?", is stuck in my head I feel like it's going to replace me saying Hello to people IRL. The game is entirely addicting to it's core. Jumping in with a group of strangers taking down a ARC is so fulfilling. I really can't put words on the social aspect of this game, but it feels like a awesome experiment.

When it comes to gameplay the controls feel great, everything feels great really. Graphics are really good, but not astonishing, not cutting edge, but damn good. Que times can be long on the weekends but once your in your in.

Grab a friend and get topside, the money is WELL WORTH IT! You will for sure have a blast, just don't put your gun down to strangers, always be at the ready, there is some RATS out there.

Highly recommend if you are looking for a fun, approachable, and unique extraction shooter. It's more The Division than Escape from Tarkov in terms of intensity and with 3rd person only. But as someone who highly prefers FPS, this game still hits a sweet spot with combat mechanics and gunplay. You or your squad spawn on very well-designed and unique maps with a chosen loadout of equipment, along with other players/squads. You have deadly AI enemies (ARC) on the map and can fight other players to take their loot. Get loot and extract before the timer is up, that is the main goal each round. Rounds are short, lasting 20-30 minutes, making for some short, casual sessions if that's your thing.

It's still an evolving meta with the PvPvE, but expect now more of a focus on PvP, you cannot expect that each round will be full of friendlies who'll let you PvE and run straight to quests items. Using your mic to flex your charisma points is super-fun, when it works. You need awareness of your surroundings and understand that the ARC should not be you're only focus, it's also awareness of the players. Yes, extract campers, betrayers, and griefers exist, just with any other extraction shooter. The way you play the game needs to adjust to that, not the other way around.

The looting aspect is solid, with plenty of diverse types of loot that get you through quests and to use to build equipment and guns. There's tons of weapons that are all pretty much viable and have their uses, save for a few exceptions. There's various types of utility that give much more depth to combat, with different types of mines, grenades, and barriers you can deploy.

The developers seem to be on-top of updates with content thus far, as they have already released a new map, just a few weeks after release. Be aware there are balancing tweaks that they're still figuring out, with some changes for the better and for worse (mainly gun balancing). The performance and optimization of the game is quite amazing and they've really figured out how to use Unreal Engine 5 without performance hitches normally associated.

Speaking of endgame, the quest line is rather arbitrary, with so-so rewards and a loose storyline (as cinematic short videos) as you progress. It mainly serves to get you to explore the map and go to areas you would normally not go to. I'd suggest not using guides for the quests, but some of them are very tricky (frustrating) to figure out, especially if you die due to PvP and have to restart. There really is no fanfare when you complete the questline. There are side missions you can work on and most have started just to PvP at this point.

The hype is real, it's a well-designed multiplayer game, very fun and addicting to play!

ARC Raiders – 100% Achievement and Game Completion Review (125 Hours)

SECTION 1 — Should You Play This Game, and Is the 100% Worth It?
I hit level 75 (Max level - final achievement) and 100%'d ARC Raiders at about 125 hours total. Someone focusing on XP from the start could probably do it in closer to 100 hours if they are aggressively grinding
The achievement difficulty is around a 2 out of 5 in terms of skill. Nothing felt mechanically tough or challenging if you're comfortable with shooter games. The real challenge is simply time and learning the game. The max-level achievement is the grindy one (and I say that lightly compared to other big games), a couple achievements can bug out, but after a second attempt I was able to get the three that did bug (might have been user error). Some quests benefitted from random players to help which can be frustrating but in solos I found most people surprisingly cooperative.
Aside from achievements there are many things to do in game. looting for specific gear, a free "battle pass", a series of challenges in game you can do that refresh weekly for rewards (trials - do them), specific quest that render cosmetic and in game items (no XP given though - hoping this changes), and obviously PVP.
So, should you get into ARC Raiders?
1. If you enjoy PVP style games - Yes
2. If you enjoy playing a game naturally with no missable achievements - Yes
3. If you have realistically 100-150 hours to dump into a game - Yes.
4. If you want a game with a lot of different things to do and ways to play - Yes
5. If you like Devs who listen to the community and make changes - Yes
6. If you want to enjoy a community that's still fresh and growing - Yes
The world is beautiful, dangerous, and unpredictable. The tension is constant, the loop is addicting, and both players and AI feel like real threats. The only “downside” is the social chaos of fake friendlies who later shoot you in the back for your stuff, and honestly, it's part of the charm of what makes this game so great. 
SECTION 2 — For People Starting the Grind or Curious About My Experience
The first 30 hours for me went by fast as I was learning how to craft, manage loadouts, materials, weapon scaling, etc. These all will take a lot of time to learn. Normally I pick up guides, but I played at launch, so any guides would have been near worthless anyway with clickbait ("NEW BEST WAY TO LOOT" - the guy who's played the game for 6 hours). ARC Raiders throws a lot at you at once. So, when you understand the systems, the game gets smoother and each run feels more intentional.
At 50 hours I had a good handle on the game, what gave me the most XP, and how to accomplish it safely (looting big enemies, scavenging in every bin, and lasting as long as you can on topside).
Around the 80 hours mark I had the game completely down to best loot paths, how to run for different items I needed, what gear works best for different maps, what fights to take and not take.
At the 100-hour mark and final push, I completed everything, but that max level achievement and the game slowed down dramatically. It was still fun, but the focus on my level made the XP seem like it was coming in slower even though it wasn't.
If I could start over, the biggest tips I’d give myself are simple: dismantle items in game you don't need to low-tier material, upgrade low-tier weapons going in (they’re much stronger than they look), stick with level 1 bags for the weight/space (in early game), practice PVP with the free loadouts, and don’t play paranoid the whole time. The game is about risk/reward when your gear is worth nothing, yet strong because of easy weapon upgrades you have little to lose but everything to gain. And I can't stress this enough, help kill big guys and LOOT EVERYTHING. that's where the real XP comes in.
Finally, my gripes: the skill trees are okay but could use some tuning, and since you can’t respec yet, it’s worth watching a quick overview before dumping points and wasting them (this is being actively worked on by devs) Once you’ve done everything, the loop can start to feel slow when you have nothing to go for, forcing PVP, but that’s really only because I binged the game hard in a short time. More content is coming anyway so it shouldn't be a problem for anyone picking up the game now. And as mentioned before, fake "friendlies."
I loved this game, and even though I've finished everything I will continue playing it once more content comes out (probably at a slower rate as I have other achievement grinds I'm working on). If you have any questions, I'll happily answer them! Good luck Raiders and see you topside.
